LESSON: CONSERVING LEFT-OVER FOODS (REHEATING OR PREPARING ANOTHER RECIPE TO AVOID WASTAGE)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Conserving Left-over Foods (Reheating or preparing another recipe to avoid wastage)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Conserving Left-over Foods (Reheating or preparing another recipe to avoid wastage), part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How is left over food prepared for use to prevent food wastage? 2. Why is it important to conserve leftover foods at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Conserving Left-over Foods (Reheating or preparing another recipe to avoid wastage) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner develop assessment and decision-making skills as they assess the environment

to identify ways of conserving left-over food.

• Creativity and imagination: Experimenting skills as the learner explore different ways of preparing left over foods.

Values:
• Unity: as the learner works together with peers to conserve left-over foods.

• Integrity: as the learner avoids wasteful use of resources.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Environmental awareness and protection: The learner analyses and designs ways conserving left over foods.

• Hygiene: The learner handles food to prevent wastage and contamination.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• The learner relates conservation of leftover foods to spread of food related communicable diseases learnt through Integrated

Science.

6

and makes a model to depict integrated farming enterprise.

Values:

• Respect: as the learner appreciates other’s opinions while conducting activities in integrated farming.

cardboards and papers to design and make a model of integrated farming enterprise.

Core competencies to be developed:


  -  Learning to learn: learners develop the skill of organising own learning as they engage the community and learn techniques of

growing crops without use of agro-chemicals.


  -  Self-efficacy: as learners execute their plans in preparation and use of organic foliar feed in organic farming practices.

Values:


  -  Unity: as learners work as a team and cooperate with the community to acquire information on organic farming practices.


  -  Peace: as learners work in consultation and harmony in the organic farming practices.

Pertinent and contemporary issues:


  -  Food health and safety: as learners acquire skills of growing foods without use of agro-chemicals.

Links to other subjects:


  -  Learners relate organic gardening practices to farming practices in the Social Studies.
